图像 6 槽：默认启用 1。音频 3 槽、视频 1 槽：默认关闭。
请用左侧多组开关启用已上传的素材；不要开启空槽。
输出保留 24 fps，时长换算沿用原版 17n+5 对齐。
“7 秒”会对齐为 175 帧，成片约 7.29 秒。
图像/音频/视频总量及格式限制以云端 H3 节点为准。

nodes.title: 稀疏注意力 · 原参数

widgets_values:
subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the male protagonist from <Picture 1>. Preserve his exact facial identity, short textured black hair, thick eyebrows, brown eyes, defined jawline, natural skin texture, and small facial moles. He is bare-chested, wearing plain black boxing shorts, dark boxing shoes, red boxing gloves, and white wrist wraps.
<Subject 2> is the distinct male opponent shown in <Picture 2>, preserving his short dark hair, facial stubble, muscular bare upper body, red gloves, and white wrist wraps.
<Picture 2> defines the opening frame of [Shot 1], continuing directly from the preceding segment's final image: the opponent's extended red glove approaches the protagonist's viewpoint inside the ring.

summary:
[reference generation + keyframe completion] A ten-second continuation begins at the incoming punch, follows <Subject 1>'s disoriented first-person perception after impact, then cuts outside his viewpoint to show him losing balance and falling backward onto the canvas.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (viewpoint in [Shot 1], visible in [Shot 2] and [Shot 3]): fully_preserved - retain the protagonist's exact identity and established boxing appearance.
<Subject 2> (appears in [Shot 1] and [Shot 2]): fully_preserved - maintain the opponent's separate identity and appearance.
<Picture 2> ([Shot 1] opening frame): fully_preserved - continue its glove position, opponent placement, ring geometry, and overhead lighting without restarting the punch.

detailed_description:
Live-action boxing feature-film realism. Exactly ten seconds. Continue the same ring, lighting, costumes, perspiration, and predominantly European and North American audience. Real-time physical action with brief subjective perceptual effects.

[Shot 1] Begin directly from <Picture 2>, at the endpoint of the opponent's incoming straight punch. The camera represents <Subject 1>'s eyes.

0.0–0.4 seconds:
Complete the final few centimeters of the existing punch. A single heavy impact jolts the viewpoint sharply backward and slightly upward. The red glove briefly overwhelms the near foreground, then withdraws naturally. Do not repeat the wind-up or introduce another punch.

0.4–3.0 seconds:
The protagonist's perception becomes unstable. Overhead lights stretch softly out of focus. Ring ropes briefly appear as two slightly misregistered layers, then partially reunite. The horizon rolls a few degrees as his balance fails. The opponent remains recognizably one person rather than becoming duplicated bodies.

Use fluctuating focus, restrained peripheral darkening, and short-lived optical ghosting to express dizziness. These are subjective visual effects, not a transformation of the ring. Crowd noise becomes distant and heavily muffled as waves of internal ringing rise and fall.

[Shot 2] At 00:03.000, hard cut to an objective lateral medium-wide shot showing <Subject 1>'s complete body, his feet, the opponent, and the canvas behind him.

3.0–5.0 seconds:
His knees soften. His guard drops unevenly. He attempts one short backward recovery step but cannot bring his feet beneath his shifting center of mass. His expression is unfocused, with his mouthguard still in place.

5.0–7.5 seconds:
He falls backward under gravity. His torso tilts, his hips descend, and his gloved hands separate reflexively. The opponent stays standing and does not strike again.

Show one continuous, physically coherent fall. His upper back and shoulder reach the canvas first, immediately followed by a heavy contact of the back of his head against the padded surface. The head contact is clearly visible once. The canvas depresses subtly beneath his weight, and his body settles with a small natural rebound.

No airborne launch, neck twisting, impossible body rotation, or repeated impact.

[Shot 3] At 00:07.500, cut to a low close-up beside the fallen protagonist's head.

7.5–10.0 seconds:
His head rests against the canvas, turned slightly toward the camera so his identity remains clear. Perspiration catches the overhead light. His eyes struggle briefly to focus, then hold an unfixed gaze. His chest continues moving with shallow, visible breathing. One red glove rests near the lower edge of the frame.

The ropes and moving audience remain softly blurred behind him. End while he is still on the canvas, overwhelmed by the ringing. No recovery, dialogue, or second fall.

Preserve the protagonist's face during impact and after landing. Maintain connected limbs, realistic glove weight, stable ring geometry, and consistent light direction. No blood, visible wounds, broken teeth, facial deformation, bone-crunch effects, slow motion, subtitles, or watermarks.

overall_soundscape:
Begin with one dense padded punch impact. Immediately reduce the crowd into distant, low-pass-filtered sound. Introduce an internal high ringing tone layered with a low humming pressure that repeatedly swells and recedes. During the fall, retain faint shoe friction and glove movement. The single heavy canvas landing briefly interrupts the ringing with a low, muffled thud, after which the wavering hum returns over close breathing. No new bell, commentary, or dialogue.
